title: India and West Indies Brace for High-Scoring Decider in Bengaluru
excerpt: Locked 2-2 after a run-soaked series, India host West Indies in the fifth T20I at the Chinnaswamy on October 17, with Shai Hope's wicket likely to decide it — if the rain stays away.
body:
• India and West Indies are locked 2-2 heading into the fifth and final T20I in Bengaluru on Saturday, October 17, at the M. Chinnaswamy Stadium.
  • The series has been played at a run rate of 11.49, with 98 sixes already hit, and Bengaluru's short boundaries point to another high-scoring game.
  • Shai Hope has been the decisive figure: India have won every match in which they dismissed him and lost every match in which he finished unbeaten.
  • Rain is forecast for Bengaluru and could interrupt the finale, with dew also expected to favour the side chasing.

A decider few expected

India and West Indies meet in Bengaluru on Saturday for a fifth T20I that will decide a series neither side has been able to control. The five-match series stands at 2-2 after West Indies won the fourth game in Hyderabad by 24 runs, defending 247 to level the contest, according to ESPNcricinfo's preview. India won the first match by eight wickets and the third by 14 runs, while West Indies took the second by six wickets.

West Indies arrived as clear underdogs, ranked seventh in T20Is, and had not beaten India in India in a series in any format since 2002. A win in Bengaluru would also make them the first visiting side to win a T20I series in India since February 2019. For India, playing without Jasprit Bumrah and Hardik Pandya, the finale is a test of a bowling attack that has conceded totals above 240 twice in the series.

Why the runs keep coming

The numbers explain the tone of the preview coverage. ESPNcricinfo notes that no series or tournament longer than three matches has been scored at a faster rate than this one, and the 98 sixes hit so far are closing on the bilateral full-member record of 120. Sports Digest makes the same point about Bengaluru itself: good bounce, a fast outfield and short boundaries, with an average first-innings score around 180 or higher in T20 cricket at the ground.

That combination is why team selection has become a debate about wickets rather than containment. India are expected to retain the XI that played in Hyderabad, with the small ground again counting against leg-spinner Kuldeep Yadav. Former players have argued the opposite case — that only a wicket-taking spinner can slow West Indies — but the preview reporting suggests India will stay unchanged unless the pitch looks unusually dry and helpful for turn.

Hope against Samson, Chase against the left-handers

Shai Hope's tour has shaped everything. He is the leading run-scorer in the T20I series and has scored four centuries across the full tour of India, including an unbeaten hundred in Hyderabad. ESPNcricinfo's stark split — India winning when Hope is out, losing when he is not — frames the decider as, in large part, a contest to dismiss him early.

India's counter is at the top of the order. Sanju Samson has scored two half-centuries in the series and, crucially, has attacked off-spinner Roston Chase, who has otherwise troubled left-handers Abhishek Sharma and Ishan Kishan, dismissing each of them twice while conceding under a run and a half per ball to them. If Samson can neutralise Chase in the powerplay again, India's left-handers get an easier entry. If Chase strikes early, West Indies control the middle overs.

West Indies also have a form bowler of their own. Keemo Paul took five wickets in Hyderabad and has eight in the series, giving captain Hope a genuine strike option on a ground where most bowlers have simply tried to survive.

Probable teams and conditions

India's probable XI is Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson, Ishan Kishan, captain Shreyas Iyer, Tilak Varma, Naman Dhir, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel, Prince Yadav, Mayank Yadav and Arshdeep Singh. West Indies are expected to keep Jewel Andrew at the top after he replaced Kamil Pooran, and to retain Romario Shepherd after his return from injury and fast bowler Shamar Joseph despite an expensive economy rate, for lack of another pace option of his type.

The match starts at 7:00 p.m. IST. The one factor neither captain controls is the weather. Forecasts point to rain interruptions, possibly significant ones, which would raise the value of the toss, shorten calculations for the side batting second, and could turn a run feast into a sprint.

What it means for diaspora fans

For Indian fans in North America, the decider starts Saturday morning — 6:30 a.m. Pacific and 9:30 a.m. Eastern — making it a rare live India finale that does not require staying up overnight. Bengaluru, weather permitting, is set up for one more very large score.
